title: [Livestream 12/11/2024] How elderly people in the United States spent their free time
prompt: The graph below shows how elderly people in the United States spent their free time between 1980 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph describes how older citizens in the United States used their relaxation time on 5 different activities from the 1980s to 2010s.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, it is clear that overall most of the activities saw an upward trend during the period shown, with the exception of going to the theater. It is also noteworthy that watching TV was the most popular for the largest part of the period, while the opposite was the case for browsing the Internet.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding hobbies that can be enjoyed at home, in 1980, exactly 60% of the American elderly watched TV in their free time, double the figure for reading, while only a negligible 5% chose to go online. In the subsequent years, both watching TV and surfing the Internet gained in popularity, before diverging in the last decade, ending up at 65% and 50%, respectively. Reading, however, fluctuated wildly until 2000, before rising dramatically to 60% in 2010.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With respect to other activities, at the beginning of the period, half of the elderly went to the theater for relaxation, whereas the number of people choosing hiking was 20%. Subsequently, after bottoming out at 30% in 1990, theater's numbers recovered in the remaining years to 45% in 2010. On the other hand, the figures for hiking went up sharply, finishing as the most popular hobby, at 80%.
